chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both), who said:

The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his Family, said: 'Do not be deceived by the one who extends his upper arms with blood, for indeed, he will have from Allah a killer that does not die.' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, and what is a killer that does not die?' He said: 'The Fire.'

key_terms.بِالدَّمِ: With blood, referring to killing or shedding blood
key_terms.رَحْبُ الذِّرَاعَيْنِ: The one with broad arms, metaphorically meaning one who kills easily or frequently
key_terms.قَاتِلًا لَا يَمُوتُ: A killer that does not die, referring to an eternal or perpetual form of death

ai.seo_question: What is the 'killer that does not die' mentioned in the hadith?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, linking the ease of killing to the severity of the eternal punishment. The phrase 'killer who does not die' signifies that while the physical killer dies, his soul remains in Hellfire, a concept deeply resonant in Shia exegesis regarding the permanence of divine retribution for unjust bloodshed.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammed bin Isa, from Hussain bin Sa’eed, from Muhammed bin Abi ‘Umayr, from Mansur bin Yunus, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Ali bin Hussain, peace be upon them both, that he said:

The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said: Verily, do not be lured by the one who extends his upper arms with blood, for indeed, he will have, from Allah, a killer that does not die. They said: O Messenger of Allah, and what is a killer that does not die? He said: The Fire.
